ac2ColumnDriftDisposition.headline: The 27 are 27 DIAGNOSTICS across 6 (table, column) PAIRS, not 27 distinct objects. The brief and the AC both say '27 column drifts'; the measurement behind them is DB-008's scoped tsc run, which reports 6 pairs summing to exactly 27 column-drift diagnostics (9+8+7+1+1+1). ac2ColumnDriftDisposition.sourceOfTheNumber: docs/engineering/DB008_RECONCILIATION_MATRIX.json -> columnDrift.absentFromChainAndContract_noRegenerationCanFix_these. DB-008's own reading of that set: 'These are the code-drift class: the product code selects a column that no active migration creates and that the contract does not declare. No regeneration can ever satisfy them.' DB-008 also records that the broader bucket is 331 unclosable Supabase-object diagnostics = 27 column-drift diagnostics (these 6 pairs) + 304 relation-literal diagnostics (72 literals). ac2ColumnDriftDisposition.measurementCaveatCarriedForward: DB-008's numbers come from a SCOPED tsc run over 1,113 roots (every file under app/, lib/, components/ and types/ containing `.select(`), not a full-repo typecheck, and it was measured on a different worktree with concurrent lanes. The pair list was re-verified on disk for this file — every relation and every canonical replacement below was read out of `lib/database.types.ts` and the active chain at this SHA — but the DIAGNOSTIC COUNTS are DB-008's and were not re-measured here, because a full typecheck is prohibited on this machine (68m18s on CI, OOMs locally, shared box). dispositionVocabulary: canonical-replacement: a column that DOES exist, in the chain and in the contract. The consumer names the wrong column; the fix is to name the right one. Owner is the lane that owns the consumer. This is the only category the database lane may act on, and it did not act on any of them, because every fix is an edit to a file in another lane's working set.
dead-consumer: the consumer is wrong in a way that no column can satisfy, so the column must not be created. Adding one would be the database lane inventing a product contract.
accepted-debt: a real, understood gap where the correct answer is known but is not this task's to take, recorded with its owner so the residual count has a name rather than a number.

ac3ChainBuiltRegenerationTarget.criterion: AC-3 — record the exact chain-built target procedure and its verification, so regeneration becomes a single command once a target exists.
ac3ChainBuiltRegenerationTarget.theVerdictThisProcedureImplements: CP-127, recorded in docs/engineering/DB008_RECONCILIATION_MATRIX.json -> regenerationTargetVerdict: lib/database.types.ts was generated from a CHAIN-BUILT database — the active numbered chain applied in version order — watermarked at 20260910000001_get_active_organizer_account_for_org.sql. The admissible source is a chain-built target and ONLY a chain-built target. `--linked` is PERMANENTLY DISQUALIFIED, and the disqualification does not rest on its size: the committed contract has ZERO out-of-band relations, columns and callables against the chain, so a target with 78 relations and 112 columns the chain never creates is by definition not the contract's source, whatever its size.
ac3ChainBuiltRegenerationTarget.whyTheCommandIsAlreadySafeToPoint: `scripts/ci/generate-database-types.mjs:16` now passes `maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024`. The earlier wave recorded that this call site had NO maxBuffer, so Node's 1 MB cap applied and the generator failed with ENOBUFS (errno -55) on any target, against a 1.18 MB payload. That defect is CLOSED in the current tree and was re-read here rather than carried forward from the older record. `scripts/ci/database-types-source.mjs` is the single place the source is chosen, and it accepts exactly `local`, `linked` and `project-id`; `linked` is admissible as a MECHANISM and inadmissible as a SOURCE, which is why the procedure below never names it.

routeA_localStack.status: DOCUMENTED, NOT EXECUTED. DB-019's brief forbids attempting `supabase start` on this machine, and it was not attempted.
routeA_localStack.whenItBecomesAvailable: `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` reported 17 GiB free on a 228 GiB volume at 92% capacity when this task ran, against roughly 10 GB of Supabase local stack images. DB-008 measured 6.7 GiB free and recorded the stack as unbuildable. The capacity fact has CHANGED in this task's favour and the route is no longer blocked on disk — it is blocked only on the instruction not to attempt it.
commands: # 0. Free nothing further and pull nothing. 17 GiB free is sufficient for the local stack.
# 1. Build a BRAND-NEW local stack. The CLI applies supabase/migrations/ in version order on first start,
#    which is the DEFINITION of a chain-built target rather than a replay of an existing database.
#    CP-051 forbids `supabase db reset` and forced/full-chain replays of a database that already exists;
#    it does not forbid creating a new one from the chain. Confirm the apply log lists every migration.
supabase start
# 2. PROVE THE STACK IS CHAIN-BUILT BEFORE GENERATING FROM IT. This is the step that makes the route
#    safe rather than hopeful: a developer stack that has had SQL pasted into it by hand is NOT
#    admissible, because its provenance is unknown and DB-002 has recorded that some versions on
#    hosted targets were applied by raw Management API SQL.
node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs . /tmp/db008/replay-local.json
#    PASS requires: outOfBandColumns 0, outOfBandRelations 0, contractOnlyRelations 0,
#    contractOnlyRoutines 0, contractReproducibleFromChain true.
#    If any of those is non-zero, STOP: the stack is not chain-built and must not be generated from.
# 3. Generate. One command, CP-016, the canonical path.
npm run generate:database-types
# 4. Verify in both directions. check-database-types re-runs the generator and compares byte-for-byte,
#    so it proves reproducibility; the replay proves the direction of the delta.
npm run check:database-types
node supabase/tests/db008_contract_attribution_audit.mjs .
bash supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh
routeA_localStack.expectedResult: SUPERSEDED BY `measuredAfterDB019`, which was measured on the real repository with DB-019's three files in the chain rather than projected. The direction is unchanged and is the one that matters: a chain-built regeneration is ADDITIVE ONLY, 402 -> 431 relations, 5,275 -> 5,341 columns, 100 -> 143 callables, and it DELETES 0 relations, 0 columns and 0 callables. The deletion direction staying at 0 is the property the replay exists to protect, and a regeneration that deletes anything means the target was not chain-built.
routeA_localStack.theStepThatIsEasyToSkipAndMustNotBe: Step 2. Generating from an unproven stack reproduces exactly the failure CP-127 was written to prevent, and it is silent: the generator succeeds, the file is rewritten, and the loss is only visible afterwards in a diff nobody reads.

routeB_isolatedStagingProject.status: THE ROUTE THAT ACTUALLY UNBLOCKS CI. Provisioning is release/ops's action and is not this lane's; the procedure below is written so that the operator's work is one script and one review, not a judgement call.
routeB_isolatedStagingProject.whyItIsTheBetterRoute: It needs no local disk, it is reproducible by anyone, and it is the only route on which the generated contract can be produced on a machine that will also run `npm run check:database-types` in CI. Route A produces a contract that only the machine with the stack can verify.
commands: # 1. Provision an ISOLATED, EMPTY staging project. release/ops owns this. It must be empty: this route
#    builds a target, and the whole admissibility argument rests on there being nothing to inherit.
# 2. APPLY THE CHAIN ONE MIGRATION AT A TIME, IN VERSION ORDER, STOPPING ON THE FIRST FAILURE.
#    This is CP-051's prescribed shape, not a violation of it: CP-051 forbids `supabase db reset`,
#    `db push --include-all` and forced/full-chain replays. Applying 320 reviewed files one at a time,
#    each reviewed and explicit, on a database that did not exist a minute ago, IS the manual apply
#    CP-051 requires. `--include-all` is the thing being avoided, and it is not used.
export STAGING_DB_URL='postgresql://...:5432/postgres'
for f in $(ls supabase/migrations/*.sql | sort); do
echo "== applying $f"
psql "$STAGING_DB_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f "$f" || { echo "STOP at $f"; break; }
done
# 3. PROVE THE APPLIED HISTORY IS THE CHAIN, not something that resembles it.
supabase migration list --db-url "$STAGING_DB_URL"
#    PASS requires: every version under supabase/migrations/ is listed as applied, and nothing else is.
#    A version MISSING here is the CP-104/DB-008 out-of-band class and must be investigated, not skipped.
# 4. Generate from the project, with an explicit source. Never `linked`.
export SUPABASE_TYPE_SOURCE=project-id
export SUPABASE_TYPE_PROJECT_ID='<the project ref, 8-64 lowercase alphanumerics>'
npm run generate:database-types
# 5. Verify.
npm run check:database-types
node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs . /tmp/db008/replay-staging.json
node supabase/tests/db008_contract_attribution_audit.mjs .
npm run agents:validate
routeB_isolatedStagingProject.knownObstacleRecordedNotWorkedAround: Ten active migrations create `storage.objects` policies, and `CREATE POLICY` enforces `pg_class_ownercheck`, which a replay role satisfies only as the exact owner, a superuser, or a member of the owning role. Under a non-owner replay role the chain ABORTS at the first of them. DB-013's lane applied the CP-059 subtransaction-guard pattern to all ten (10/10 harness scenarios pass), so a replay role that is neither the owner nor a superuser should now complete the chain and report a `sqlstate`/`sqlerrm` WARNING for each policy it could not create. The operator should run the replay AS the table owner or as a superuser, which is the ordinary case for a fresh project, and should READ the warnings rather than treat them as success: a warning per policy is the guard working, and a policy set that is materially smaller than the chain's is a target whose provenance is not the chain. `supabase/tests/db008_storage_replay_guard.harness.sh` is the reference for what a correct outcome looks like.

verificationThatTheProcedureActuallyWork: `npm run check:database-types` — re-runs the generator against the SAME source and compares byte-for-byte with the committed file. This is the reproducibility proof: it is what makes the committed contract a function of the chain rather than of one moment.

`node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs . <out>` — the direction proof. `outOfBandColumns`, `outOfBandRelations`, `contractOnlyRelations` and `contractOnlyRoutines` must ALL be 0 after regeneration. A non-zero value in any of them means the target had surface the chain does not create, and the regenerated contract now encodes a database this repository cannot reproduce.

`node supabase/tests/db008_contract_attribution_audit.mjs .` — every contract column must be attributable to a named active migration that mentions both the relation and the column. 5,170 attributions with 0 unsupported at this SHA; the count will rise with the regenerated file and the ZERO is the assertion.

`bash supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh` — 8 PASS lines when `DB_LINKED_TYPES` is unset, and the assertion must be on the per-harness PASS lines rather than the runner's own summary counter, which DB-008 measured as wrong (`ran 9, skipped 1, failed 0` after executing EIGHT harnesses, because `ran` is incremented before the skip check).

A SCOPED typecheck, not a full one — the same shape DB-008 used: every file under app/, lib/, components/ and types/ containing `.select(` as tsconfig `files[]`, run with `--noEmit --noErrorTruncation`. `--noErrorTruncation` is not optional: tsc abbreviates a long union as `... 380 more ...`, and that abbreviation is what made 29 of DB-008's 173 SelectQueryError lines unrecoverable. The expected movement after regeneration is the 76 closable diagnostics (60 column-drift across 3 pairs, plus 16 relation-literal across 4 literals) going to zero. The 27 in this file and the 304 relation-literal diagnostics do NOT move, which is precisely why they needed an owner.
ac3ChainBuiltRegenerationTarget.theHardRuleAndWhyItIsWrittenDown: `--linked` must never be used as a generation source for this repository, and the reason is a SET relationship rather than a size, so it cannot be argued away by a target that happens to be smaller. The committed contract has zero out-of-band relations, columns and callables against the active chain. A target carrying 78 relations and 112 columns that no active migration creates is, by that single property, not the contract's source — no matter how many relations it has. Regenerating from it would delete 78 relations, 112 columns and 27 callables and add 285 relations of which 276 no active migration creates. CP-016 exists to prevent exactly that, silently.
ac3ChainBuiltRegenerationTarget.whoOwnsTheNextAction: release/ops, for whether a chain-built target is provisioned at all. DB-019 owns the IDENTITY of the source, which CP-127 determined from evidence, and does not own the provisioning. The mechanical blocker is recorded in the same place DB-008 recorded it: no local stack can be built without roughly 10 GB of free disk, and this machine's free space changed from 6.7 GiB to 17 GiB during the task, so route A is now capacity-feasible and route B remains the route that unblocks CI.

db019ColumnsAreVisibleToTheGate.howVerified: All five appear in the replay report's staleColumns list with createdIn = this task's file, which means the CP-016 instrument resolved them out of a multi-clause `add column if not exists` statement rather than treating the statement as one column.
